correctness.rationale: The published d=1 formula yields weights (-1,2,-2,1). Exact algebra gives the rational cardinal functions and converts monotone bounded data to a simplex whose vertices are controlled by cumulative cardinal coefficients. Sign analysis isolates one edge coefficient; its derivative quartic has exactly one zero in (0,1), and a separate analytic estimate proves the middle-cell defect is smaller. Reflection gives the matching upper defect. Exact replay verifies all critical rational identities, algebraic brackets, and the strict witness.

value.rationale: Floater–Hormann interpolation is used precisely to obtain stable pole-free rational interpolation on equispaced data, yet bounded monotone tables can still leave their physical range. A complete sharp defect of more than eighteen percent on the first genuinely rational four-node d=1 stencil is a natural and reusable safety fact. The result provides exact extremizers, a strict monotone counterexample, and a closed algebraic constant rather than a qualitative plot.
